newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asian traders see LME copper prices slipping.
newsitem.headline: Asian traders see LME copper prices slipping.

text.p: Copper prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME) may slip further towards the next support level of around $2,360-70 as funds are expected to place more sell orders, Asian traders said on Wednesday.
"If the $2,400 level is breached, it might slump towards $2,360-70, the downside in an upward trend started September last year," said a trader at one of Japan's major trading houses.

At 0140 GMT, benchmark three-month copper was quoted at $2,406/11 per tonne, well below the London close of $2,437 and a five-week low of $2,430. It shed $74 in London overnight amid signs the worst of the supply tightness might have passed.
The aluminium price was $1,565/70, slightly below the London close of $1,577. The zinc price was $1,390/95, compared with the London close of $1,397 after shooting up to 6-3/4 year highs on Monday.
Traders said aluminium and zinc were likely to show more resilience despite Tuesday's retreat in line with copper.
"Zinc has firm support at $1,380. I don't think it is looking downwards. It will start moving upwards again after consolidation," said one trader.
Traders said aluminium had also strong support at around $1,550/60 where users were expected to buy.

"There are hardly any sellers," said the trader. "Although the physical market in the United States is easing, the Japanese and European markets remain tight. People have not paid much attention but warehouse stocks are still dropping."
